stability: Every entry in `outputs` is stable API: labels, basenames, and the field names/nesting shown in each example. Removing or renaming any of them is a breaking change and requires a TOOL_VERSION bump plus a changelog note here. Files NOT listed here (input_params.json, request.jsonl, _progress.json, anything under batch/) are internal and may change or vanish without notice. `description` is one line by design — it is joined verbatim into each get_job_status outputs[] entry as `desc`.

response.description: One line per input record, in request order — output_text is the model's answer; a FAILED line carries reason instead and the run still SUCCEEDS (partial success is success)

example.output_text: A flowchart of circular nodes connected by solid and dashed arrows.

response.notes: status is SUCCESS or FAILED. A FAILED line keeps record_id ordering and adds `reason` (output_text empty, stop_reason empty); usage/rounds are still reported because a record that failed after burning tokens on two models cost real money. `rounds` counts billable model calls behind the line — retries and chain fallbacks included — so summing rounds can exceed the record count. stop_reason `max_tokens` is a normal outcome with partial text intact, not an error. `notes` (optional list) records in-band recoveries, e.g. a model rejecting `temperature`. estimated_cost is null for unpriced models, never 0.0.

summary.description: Run-level rollup — which mode ran and why, per-record success counts, model fallbacks used, and the token/cost totals across every billable call
summary.notes: inference_mode is `sync` or `batch` — decided at PLAN time and reported with mode_reason (e.g. an auto decision by the dollar guard, or a requested batch downgraded to sync because the model cannot batch); never assume the mode you asked for is the mode that ran. failures[] lists EVERY failed record as {record_id, reason} — no truncation (only the exception MESSAGE on an all-failed run caps at 5). quota_table is always present (empty string unless the deployment names an external quota table) — the split-brain detector between plan and lease. records_resumed counts records a checkpoint re-entry (or a batch repair pass) skipped as already done. bedrock_usage.cost_is_complete false means at least one round ran on an unpriced model, so estimated_cost is a floor, not the bill. `records_repaired` and `repair_error` appear only on batch runs that took the repair tail.

usage.description: Per-state Lambda wall-clock and cost accounting for the whole execution tree (orchestrator plus whichever child ran) — Bedrock spend included, for the run's total cost of ownership
usage.notes: This stack's usage state walks TWO execution histories — the orchestrator's own and whichever child ran — because the orchestrator is three short Lambda calls while every Converse retry and the whole lease wait live in the child. `complete` mirrors summary's cost_is_complete — false whenever any round ran on an unpriced model, even with full history. A run whose HISTORY was unavailable returns the degraded shape {complete: false, reason} with none of the fields below; the run's outcome is unaffected and summary.json stays authoritative for Bedrock cost. `retried` counts re-invocations of the same state (invocations - 1), not failed attempts. Shapes differ slightly across stacks — do not byte-pin this file against another workflow's.
